column1: # The ledger for environment centos-9-glibc2.34 (run.sh names this host's: os id, os version, glibc).
# Measured with `reverie-examples/e2e/run.sh --write-ledger` on a CentOS Stream 9 devserver (glibc
# 2.34), all seven backends; two runs gave identical rows. A row names a program's first difference
# only. cell<TAB>backend<TAB>verdict<TAB>signature<TAB>issue (full URL); * for any cell or signature.
# Until their own issues are filed, the rows link the audit's tracking issue. The liteinst and
# in-guest-trap rows were re-measured on 2026-11-02 after runtime descriptor isolation (a461e8bf),
# with run.sh --backends ptrace,liteinst,in-guest-trap; two runs gave identical rows.
# The awk ptrace row was re-measured on 2026-11-20 on devbig014 (kernel 7.1.3, LANG=en_US.UTF-8):
# the native /proc/self/maps first read is 4082 (strace and the recorder's native runs agree in two
# validate runs), so both sides of the row moved +25 with the same -21 first-read delta as before;
# grep-passwd's ptrace row is unchanged. The maps byte counts also depend on the ambient locale
# (natively, awk's first maps read is 4037 under LC_ALL=C and 4066 under C.UTF-8), which this
# environment name does not capture; judge only under en_US.UTF-8 or re-measure with --write-ledger.
# ptrace: the tool never sees the rt_sigreturn that ends a signal handler.
sh-fork
sh-pipe
# ptrace: a /proc/self/maps read returns a different byte count, where reverie-ptrace's
# private pages show (the cause Hermit's pinned-root ledger found for grep; confirmed by strace:
# both programs open /proc/self/maps, and the ptrace maps total is +82 bytes for each).
grep-passwd
awk
# KVM: rseq answers ENOSYS (reverie-kvm refuses it), the first difference on every program.
# liteinst: the tool lives in the example preload and starts after the loader's calls (compare.rs,
# LATE_START). Then: the shell's getrandom is not seen by the tool; awk's fcntl(F_GETFL) lacks
# O_LARGEFILE; dd's and perl's first visible calls do not appear in the native record in order (no
# aligned start); grep's read of /proc/self/maps is shorter, and more reads follow, because the
# preload's mappings are listed (as for ptrace above; later, grep's sigaltstack install is refused with
# EPERM unseen by the tool, so grep runs without its SIGSEGV handler, issue 5097); sort's rt_sigaction queries (NULL new action)
# never reach the tool (issue 5096); and a guest's own execve is refused with EOPNOTSUPP, the in-guest
# runtime not forwarding it, so python3 (run through env) exits 126 (issue 5094; sh-fork and sh-pipe
# fail the same way behind their earlier first difference, issue 5095).
grep-passwd
sort-passwd
python3
sh-builtin
sh-fork
sh-pipe
awk
dd-zero
perl
